cases.title_en: The Refill That Reuses the Bottle
cases.prompt_en:
On a pale stone counter, a frosted-glass serum bottle with a silver pump stands beside its open folding carton and a flat refill pouch. The carton back panel shows a small loop diagram and a paragraph about the refill system. The bottle front label carries the product name, volume, natural-origin claim, and a daily-use line. The pouch front carries a short specification line, and an opened leaflet beside the pump shows four numbered refill steps. Text on back panel of the folding carton under a recyclable-loop diagram reads exactly: "REFILL KEEPS THE BOTTLE ALIVE. Every empty bottle returns to a Reloop station, where it is washed, refilled, and sealed again. Choose the pouch, not a new bottle, and the glass stays with you for decades.". Text on front label of the glass bottle reads exactly: "Reloop Hydrating Serum
30 ml
92% natural-origin ingredients
Use morning and evening after cleansing.". Text on front of the refill pouch (flexible foil with a dry surface) reads exactly: "REFILL POUCH · 30 ml · 95% less plastic than a new bottle · recyclable PE-LD". Text on inner leaflet tucked beside the pump, opened to a four-step diagram reads exactly: "HOW TO REFILL:
1. Unscrew the outer cap.
2. Insert the pouch nozzle into the neck.
3. Squeeze to the neck line.
4. Wipe, close, lock.". A hand holds the refill pouch, inserting its nozzle into the open glass bottle neck, squeezing the amber serum upward until it reaches the neck line; the hand then wipes the rim, replaces the pump, and twists the collar to lock it. The text on the pouch and leaflet must be clearly legible.

cases.prompt_en: A high-ceilinged museum gallery is lit by warm daylight. Visitors walk among them, pausing to read wall texts and printed panels. A main exhibition banner hangs above the entrance, and a freestanding podium near the center holds a letterpress display. The installation changes shape over time as mechanical arms and air currents alter the surrounding forms. Text on fabric banner hung above the gallery entrance reads exactly: "Moving Matter: Forms in Transit". Text on long painted wall panel beside the first kinetic sculpture reads exactly: "What if a sculpture could remember the hand that shaped it? This exhibition gathers seven artists who build moving forms from light, sand, paper, and steel — every object is a question answered by motion.". Text on printed artist list mounted on a low display rail reads exactly: "Featuring Lena Okafor, Hiroshi Tanabe, Marta Reyes, Jonas Voss". Text on engraved brass strip above the exit door reads exactly: "Please do not touch the moving pieces — but you may walk close and let their shadows pass over you.". A visitor enters and walks the loop. As she passes the banner, a lightweight fabric wall beside her ripples and rearranges itself into a new silhouette. Near the podium, a paper strip above the type display is slowly pulled and folded by a mechanism, revealing additional lines of text. Another guest points to a wall panel; the artist list is visible. The kinetic pieces keep moving, casting shifting shadows across the written surfaces.

Another neighbor stops, reads the poster, then picks up the pledge card and signs it.

cases.title_en: Fringe by Fringe: Measuring Wavelength with a Double Slit
cases.prompt_en:
A dim optics laboratory bench holds a green laser on a rail, a double-slit aperture, and a white projection screen. A chalkboard on the wall carries a derivation in white chalk. An open laboratory notebook lies next to the setup, and a small anodized label on the laser housing identifies the laser. Text on chalkboard mounted on the lab wall reads exactly: "The bright fringes occur where the path difference between slits equals m λ.
For small angles, sin θ ≈ tan θ = Δy / L, so the wavelength is λ = d Δy / L.
The measured 533 nm agrees with the 532 nm laser label within the ±11 nm uncertainty.". Text on open laboratory notebook on the table reads exactly: "d = 0.40 mm
L = 1.80 m
Δy = (2.40 ± 0.05) mm
λ = dΔy/L = (533 ± 11) nm". Text on anodized label attached to the laser housing reads exactly: "532 nm green diode laser". The laser beam passes through the double slit, casting a steady pattern of bright and dark fringes on the screen. A hand adjusts the slit holder, then writes measured fringe spacing into the notebook and taps the chalkboard formula.

The bright fringes occur where the path difference between slits equals m λ.
For small angles, sin θ ≈ tan θ = Δy / L, so the wavelength is λ = d Δy / L.
The measured 533 nm agrees with the 532 nm laser label within the ±11 nm uncertainty.
required_text.role: explains the interference condition, small-angle approximation, and how the measured fringe spacing yields the wavelength, including agreement with the laser label.

The left bob swings, gradually slows, and almost stops while the right bob grows to a large swing; the pattern reverses as energy returns. The coupling spring stretches and relaxes each beat, and a little chalk dust trembles on the board sill.

cases.title_en: Wax Drops in Order: Fourier's Law Across Copper, Aluminum, and Steel
cases.prompt_en: On a laboratory bench, three metal rods — copper, aluminum, and steel — are clamped side by side. On the thermal imaging display, bright bands travel fastest along the copper rod. A hand records the measured drop times into the observation table.

cases.title_en: Chromosome Copy and Divide: A Magnetic Model Counts the Way
cases.prompt_en:
An evening biology teaching lab. A large projection microscope on the left bench projects an illuminated nucleus onto a wall screen, where a single cell advances through mitosis. On the black bench to the right, a detailed magnetic chromosome model kit displays four distinct, 3D duplicated chromosomes with colored chromatid halves, magnetic centromere beads, and flexible spindle fibers connecting to poles. A whiteboard on the far right wall displays a phase-record chart. Beside the model on the bench, a compact digital checkpoint panel and a printed rule card sit clearly visible. The room is otherwise dim so the projection and small task lamps define the working space. Text on projection screen of the teaching microscope reads exactly: "DNA replication doubles chromosome content from 2n to 4n, but sister chromatids remain attached at the centromere; cell division then separates them so each daughter receives one complete set of chromosomes.". Text on wall-mounted phase-evidence chart reads exactly: "Phase Evidence and Counts
Interphase: DNA copied; 2n = 4 chromosomes → 8 chromatids.
Prophase: 4 chromosomes condense, each with two chromatids.
Metaphase: 4 dyads align at equator.
Anaphase: 8 daughter chromosomes separate to opposite poles.". Text on rule card beside the magnetic chromosome model reads exactly: "Spindle Attachment Rule: Each chromosome's two kinetochores must bind microtubules from opposite poles; never from the same pole. A correct attachment produces balanced tension.". Text on compact checkpoint panel on the bench reads exactly: "SAC status: satisfied. All kinetochores occupied; no misplaced fibers; tension present. Anaphase signal ON.". A gloved hand moves the magnetic kit from one stage to the next while the projection microscope animates the same cell. The duplicated chromosomes first condense, then line up their centromeres on the equator. Motorized spindle poles extend fibers that test each kinetochore; one by one they click into place. As soon as all four chromosomes have bipolar attachments, the small checkpoint panel lights up and the projection switches from a waiting cue to an anaphase animation. The paired chromatids are pulled apart to opposite ends, the phase chart advances, and the chromosome counter on the screen changes to show two equal sets. Finally, the cell membrane pinches in two and the model is reset for the next division.

required_text.carrier: projection screen of the teaching microscope
required_text.verbatim: DNA replication doubles chromosome content from 2n to 4n, but sister chromatids remain attached at the centromere; cell division then separates them so each daughter receives one complete set of chromosomes.
required_text.form: explanatory paragraph on the projection display
required_text.role: explains why replication is followed by division in mitosis

required_text.verbatim:
Phase Evidence and Counts
Interphase: DNA copied; 2n = 4 chromosomes → 8 chromatids.
Prophase: 4 chromosomes condense, each with two chromatids.
Metaphase: 4 dyads align at equator.
Anaphase: 8 daughter chromosomes separate to opposite poles.
required_text.form: structured phase chart on wall panel
required_text.role: documents chromosome and chromatid counts by mitotic phase

required_text.carrier: rule card beside the magnetic chromosome model
required_text.verbatim: Spindle Attachment Rule: Each chromosome's two kinetochores must bind microtubules from opposite poles; never from the same pole. A correct attachment produces balanced tension.
required_text.role: specifies the bipolar spindle attachment constraint

required_text.carrier: compact checkpoint panel on the bench
required_text.verbatim: SAC status: satisfied. All kinetochores occupied; no misplaced fibers; tension present. Anaphase signal ON.
required_text.form: checkpoint status screen on compact panel
required_text.role: indicates checkpoint satisfaction and anaphase gating

cases.title_en: The Plateau Before the Drug: Reading Logistic Growth in an Incubator Log
cases.prompt_en: A stainless incubator with a glass door holds one agar plate on a wire shelf; an overhead blue light ring illuminates the plate. A motorized pipette is mounted on the exterior of the incubator door, pointing inward. Beside the incubator, a large wall-mounted laboratory display shows the same plate as a gridded simulation, with dark colony patches growing on a pale field. The display features a blue growth curve, an orange rate curve, a green vertical marker, a fitted-parameter card, a small nutrient table, and a plain-language interpretation note. The text on the Interpretation note under the growth plot reads exactly: "Logistic curve fits the data: r=0.73/h and K=9.5; N climbs from 0.6 to 8.9 by t=8h and then approaches K slowly. At t=14h, tetracycline stops further growth near 8.8, so this carrying capacity is only a pre-intervention plateau.". The text on the Model equation card reads exactly: "dN/dt = rN(1 - N/K); N = population size, r = per-capita growth rate, K = carrying capacity". The text on the Parameter readout card reads exactly: "N₀=0.6, r=0.73/h, K=9.5; exponential doubling time = ln2/r ≈ 0.95 h". The text on the Small nutrient table beside the growth curve reads exactly: "t=8h: glucose 0.42 g/L, NH₄⁺ 0.05 g/L; t=14h: glucose 0.05 g/L, NH₄⁺ 0.01 g/L". The text on the Green vertical marker on the growth plot reads exactly: "intervention: tetracycline 2.5 µg/mL added". Over the time-lapse, dark colonies on the gridded plate image enlarge and merge, while the blue curve rises and then bends toward a plateau. When the clock passes the fourteenth hour, the motorized pipette on the incubator door extends, releases one droplet of antibiotic solution onto the agar, and retracts. The green marker appears at that time, the curve stops climbing, the rate curve drops to zero, nutrient values fall gradually, and the interpretation note updates.

required_text.carrier: Interpretation note under the growth plot
required_text.verbatim: Logistic curve fits the data: r=0.73/h and K=9.5; N climbs from 0.6 to 8.9 by t=8h and then approaches K slowly. At t=14h, tetracycline stops further growth near 8.8, so this carrying capacity is only a pre-intervention plateau.
required_text.role: Explains why fitted K represents a pre-intervention plateau once tetracycline halts growth.

required_text.carrier: Model equation card on the display
required_text.verbatim: dN/dt = rN(1 - N/K); N = population size, r = per-capita growth rate, K = carrying capacity
required_text.role: States the logistic model and variable meanings used in the fit.

required_text.verbatim: N₀=0.6, r=0.73/h, K=9.5; exponential doubling time = ln2/r ≈ 0.95 h
required_text.role: Gives fitted starting population, growth rate, carrying capacity, and exponential doubling time.

required_text.carrier: Small nutrient table beside the growth curve
required_text.verbatim: t=8h: glucose 0.42 g/L, NH₄⁺ 0.05 g/L; t=14h: glucose 0.05 g/L, NH₄⁺ 0.01 g/L
required_text.role: Provides nutrient evidence for growth slowing before drug addition and nutrient depletion continuing after.

required_text.carrier: Green vertical marker on the growth plot
required_text.verbatim: intervention: tetracycline 2.5 µg/mL added
required_text.role: Marks the moment and concentration of antibiotic intervention.

cases.title_en: Counting a Meadow by Capture, Mark, Recapture
cases.prompt_en: A one-metre transparent meadow box holds artificial grass tufts and dozens of beetle-shaped tokens in several colors. A wide-mouth catching jar, a paint pen, a white sorting tray, and a field notebook rest beside it. On a nearby easel, a chalkboard, a clip-held data sheet, a small assumptions placard, and a labelled jar stand in a loose arc around the model. Text on Field notebook page reads exactly: "We marked 34 beetles in the morning catch. After mixing, the afternoon sample held 29 beetles, 11 marked. If marks do not change behavior, 11/29 = 34/N, so N ≈ 89. Small R means wide uncertainty: 95% CI 58–178.". Text on Chalkboard panel reads exactly: "N = M × C / R = 34 × 29 / 11 ≈ 89.6". Text on Data clipboard sheet reads exactly: "First catch: 34 caught, mark all, release. Second catch: 29 caught; 11 marked, 18 unmarked.". Text on Assumptions placard reads exactly: "Assumptions: closed population; marks persist; random mixing; equal catchability.". Text on Adhesive label on recapture jar reads exactly: "Bias: easier recapture → R too high → N too low.". A naturalist in a canvas apron sweeps the jar through the tufts, empties the catch into the tray, then uses the paint pen to dot each captured token. She pours the marked tokens back into the meadow and gently stirs the tufts. Later she makes another sweep, sorts the second catch into dotted and plain piles, and counts both piles. An assistant updates the chalkboard figures as each count is called out.

required_text.verbatim: We marked 34 beetles in the morning catch. After mixing, the afternoon sample held 29 beetles, 11 marked. If marks do not change behavior, 11/29 = 34/N, so N ≈ 89. Small R means wide uncertainty: 95% CI 58–178.
required_text.role: Explains the estimate and its uncertainty
Shows Lincoln–Petersen calculation

required_text.verbatim: First catch: 34 caught, mark all, release. Second catch: 29 caught; 11 marked, 18 unmarked.
required_text.role: Records the two sample counts

required_text.verbatim: Assumptions: closed population; marks persist; random mixing; equal catchability.
required_text.role: Lists model assumptions

required_text.verbatim: Bias: easier recapture → R too high → N too low.
required_text.role: Warns how bias shifts the estimate

cases.title_en: Three Drums, One Tremor: Reading the Quarry Epicenter
cases.prompt_en: On a workbench, three drum seismographs with rotating paper-covered cylinders stand around a regional relief map, and a small striker on the map frame taps a metal fault plate to produce a tremor. Curling paper strips emerge from the drums; a whiteboard and an open notebook sit behind the map. Text on printed station log card beside the first drum reads exactly: "Ashford — P 04:10, S 04:40, Δt 30 s → D 252 km". Text on printed station log card beside the second drum reads exactly: "Birchfield — P 04:16, S 04:56, Δt 40 s → D 336 km". Text on printed station log card beside the third drum reads exactly: "Cinder Hollow — P 04:02, S 04:27, Δt 25 s → D 210 km". Text on whiteboard mounted behind the map reads exactly: "D = Δt × 8.4 km/s (from Vp = 6.0 km/s, Vs = 3.5 km/s)". Text on open notebook page reads exactly: "The three circles do not meet at one point. Their overlap is a small polygon; reading uncertainty is about one second, so the polygon, not a point, is the honest answer. The epicenter then lies on the buried fault boundary south of the quarry, matching a shallow slip.". Text on small placard on the relief map at a worked-out pit reads exactly: "old quarry". After the striker taps the fault plate, pens on the three drums scratch wave arrivals. A gloved hand measures the gaps on each strip, writes station logs, draws a travel-time conversion on the whiteboard, uses compasses to draw circles from each station on the map, shades the overlapping polygon, then writes a conclusion in the notebook.

cases.title_en: The Box of Chance: Half-Life by Counting Marked Cubes
cases.prompt_en:
A warmly lit physics classroom at night. A circular luminous table is covered with hundreds of small cubes, each with a single bright face. To the left, a whiteboard carries a dense explanatory note and a sketched curve. To the right, a translucent panel shows a completed experimental record and a linearized plot with the same data. Text on whiteboard panel left of the glowing table reads exactly: "Each cube has one marked face. A roll is one decay attempt. With p = 1/6, the expected number surviving after t rolls is N = N0(1/2)^(t/T½), where T½ = 3.80 rolls. Observed counts scatter around N but do not fall exactly on the curve; the log graph makes the half-life easy to read. A single cube's next roll is unpredictable—only the crowd obeys the law.". Text on translucent log screen on the right wall reads exactly: "t   observed   expected
0   600   600
1   494   500
2   421   417
3   337   347
4   291   289
5   238   241
6   214   201". Text on chalkboard area above the fitted line reads exactly: "ln N = ln N0 − (ln 2 / T½) · t". Text on sticker on the cube storage box reads exactly: "BOX B · 600 CUBES · 1 MARKED FACE EACH". A demonstrator rolls all cubes across the glowing surface, removes every cube that lands with its designated face upward, counts the survivors, and writes the pair into the table. The remaining set is gathered and rolled again; after several rounds, the observed totals scatter around the falling expected curve, and the plot on the panel straightens when the logarithm is used.

required_text.carrier: whiteboard panel left of the glowing table
required_text.verbatim: Each cube has one marked face. A roll is one decay attempt. With p = 1/6, the expected number surviving after t rolls is N = N0(1/2)^(t/T½), where T½ = 3.80 rolls. Observed counts scatter around N but do not fall exactly on the curve; the log graph makes the half-life easy to read. A single cube's next roll is unpredictable—only the crowd obeys the law.
required_text.role: ties the probability model, half-life formula, observed scatter, and unpredictability of individual decay into one interpretation

required_text.carrier: translucent log screen on the right wall
required_text.role: records the observed survivors and the theoretical expected survivors after each roll for direct comparison

required_text.carrier: chalkboard area above the fitted line
required_text.verbatim: ln N = ln N0 − (ln 2 / T½) · t
required_text.role: shows how the exponential decay is converted into a straight-line plot from which the half-life can be read as a slope

required_text.carrier: sticker on the cube storage box
required_text.verbatim: BOX B · 600 CUBES · 1 MARKED FACE EACH
required_text.role: identifies the cube batch and states the single marked face that defines a decay event

cases.title_en: A Repelled Drop: Watching Lenz's Law in Pulse Area
cases.prompt_en:
A low teaching-lab workbench carries a transparent vertical guide tube. A black cylindrical neodymium magnet rests on a metal release pin at the top; a transparent multi-turn coil with visible copper wire turns surrounds the lower part of the tube. The coil leads run to a center-zero galvanometer and a boxed load resistor. A top-rail plaque identifies the rig, a backlit panel gives the defining equations, a clipboard sheet holds the run log, and a small explanation card is fixed below the coil. Text on An engraved aluminum plaque on the top rail reads exactly: "Lenz Response Test Rig". Text on A backlit equation panel above the coil reads exactly: "ΦB = B·A
ε = −N dΦB/dt
Pulse area = ∫ε dt = N ΔΦB
B is the field along the coil axis; A is the loop area; N = 480 turns.". Text on A clipboard data sheet mounted beside the panel reads exactly: "Run log
height cm | peak V | pulse area mWb | needle
20 | 0.44 | 3.2 | left
45 | 0.67 | 3.2 | left". Text on A small explanatory card fixed below the coil reads exactly: "When the north pole enters, the induced current makes the near coil face a north pole, so the magnet is repelled. That repulsion converts kinetic energy into Joule heat in the 4.7 Ω load; both pulse areas are 3.2 mWb, so only the flux change matters, not the entry speed.". A gloved hand pulls the release pin for the first, shorter drop; the magnet falls through the coil and the galvanometer needle kicks left before settling to zero. The hand returns the magnet, raises the release pin for a taller drop, and releases it again; the second fall makes a wider left swing, while the pulse-area value on the recorded sheet stays the same.

required_text.verbatim: Lenz Response Test Rig
required_text.role: identifies the apparatus

required_text.carrier: A backlit equation panel above the coil

ΦB = B·A
ε = −N dΦB/dt
Pulse area = ∫ε dt = N ΔΦB
B is the field along the coil axis; A is the loop area; N = 480 turns.
required_text.role: defines the flux, induced emf, and pulse-area equation with variable meanings

cases.title_en: Why the Spinning Wheel Does Not Fall: Gyroscope Precession
cases.prompt_en:
A lab bench holds a gyroscope mount on a low-friction vertical pivot. A bicycle wheel spins swiftly on a horizontal axle; on the opposite side of the axle a stack of metal discs sits on a sliding holder. A whiteboard, a data sheet on a clipboard, and a small note card rest near the apparatus. Text on whiteboard reads exactly: "τ = r × mg
L = Iω
Ω = τ/L
where r = moment arm from pivot, I = wheel's rotational inertia". Text on clipboard data sheet reads exactly: "run / m / r / period / Ω
1 / 0.50 kg / 0.25 m / 5.2 s / 1.21 rad/s
2 / 0.50 kg / 0.35 m / 3.8 s / 1.65 rad/s
3 / 0.75 kg / 0.25 m / 3.5 s / 1.80 rad/s". Text on note card on bench reads exactly: "The wheel's spin sets L along the axle. Gravity pulls the added mass downward, making torque τ perpendicular to L. This torque does not tip the axle; it shifts the direction of L, so the axle follows L and the whole assembly turns horizontally. A larger mass or longer arm increases Ω; a faster wheel decreases it. The wheel leans but never falls.". Text on sticker on mass hanger reads exactly: "adjustable mass m". The bicycle wheel spins around its axle while the whole assembly slowly rotates around the vertical pivot. The axle stays nearly horizontal, and the weighted end moves steadily along a horizontal circle; the wheel does not dip downward.

required_text.verbatim:
τ = r × mg
L = Iω
Ω = τ/L
where r = moment arm from pivot, I = wheel's rotational inertia
required_text.role: defines torque, angular momentum, and precession rate
records measured precession periods under different masses and lever arms

required_text.verbatim: The wheel's spin sets L along the axle. Gravity pulls the added mass downward, making torque τ perpendicular to L. This torque does not tip the axle; it shifts the direction of L, so the axle follows L and the whole assembly turns horizontally. A larger mass or longer arm increases Ω; a faster wheel decreases it. The wheel leans but never falls.
required_text.role: causal explanation of why the gyroscope precesses instead of falling

required_text.verbatim: adjustable mass m
required_text.role: identifies the variable mass that changes torque

cases.title_en: Wavelength Ahead, Wavelength Behind: Doppler Shift on a Teaching Rail
cases.prompt_en:
A physics laboratory table features a metal teaching rail spanning its length. A small loudspeaker mounted on a motorized cart is captured in motion, rolling steadily to the right along the rail, emitting a continuous tone. At the far left end of the rail, a microphone station labeled 'MIC A' stands on a tripod with a small digital screen; at the far right end, a microphone station labeled 'MIC B' stands similarly. Behind the table, a large green chalkboard displays handwritten text. Mounted on the wall to the left of the chalkboard is a clear acrylic explanation panel. Mounted on the wall between the chalkboard and the right microphone is a modern, translucent digital display screen that renders expanding white wavefront circles in real time; the circles are crowded ahead of the moving speaker and spread apart behind it. The room has a hands-on classroom feel with visible cable trays and chalk dust. Text on the wall-mounted acrylic explanation panel reads exactly: "An approaching source compresses wavefronts and raises the pitch ahead. The next crest leaves closer to the listener, so leading wavelengths shorten and trailing lengths stretch. The measured shift therefore traces the radial component of source velocity.". Text on a small whiteboard standing on the table between the microphone arrays reads exactly: "f_o = f_s v / (v − v_s)
f_o = f_s v / (v + v_s)". Text on a tablet on a stand beside the rail reads exactly: "f_s = 650 Hz
v_sound = 343 m/s
f_ahead = 672 Hz
f_behind = 631 Hz
λ_ahead = 0.510 m
λ_behind = 0.544 m". Text on equipment labels on the speaker cart and microphone stands reads exactly: "SOURCE
MIC A
MIC B". Text on the chalkboard behind the demonstration table reads exactly: "Use the two measured frequencies to find v_s. Explain the sign of v_s for motion toward MIC A.". The motor cart continues along the rail while the digital display adds a new wavefront circle at each emission moment. The circles bunch up in front of the cart and stretch apart behind it. On the microphone screens, the measured frequencies update; on the display, wavelength arrows shorten ahead and lengthen behind as the tone moves.

cases.title_en: The Evidence Gate: A Sorting Machine Makes Bayes Visible
cases.prompt_en:
A tall transparent sorting tower stands in a bright museum hall. A gray-aproned demonstrator turns a hand crank, and from a top hopper 1000 small discs pour down—990 gray and 10 amber—then enter a test chamber. At each pass a blue light flashes for a positive result or a red light flashes for a negative result, and flippers route the discs into a wide positive bin or a clear negative bin. Above the bin, a large translucent backlit panel displays the main text clearly. Below that, a distinct row of physical tiles shows the equation. To the side, a clear data board lists the statistics. A small plaque shows the likelihood ratio formula. Gate signs label the routes. A digital display shows the odds update. Text on the large translucent backlit panel reads exactly: "THE BASE RATE IS THE STARTING POINT
A positive result shifts the odds but does not erase the prior. With 1% prevalence, a test that finds 90% of true cases and flags 10% of healthy people takes the odds from 1:99 to 1:11. Most positives are false positives. Strong-looking evidence can leave about 92% posterior uncertainty.". Text on the distinct equation tile row reads exactly: "ODDS FORMULA
Prior odds × Likelihood ratio = Posterior odds
1 : 99 × 9 = 9 : 99 = 1 : 11". Text on the clear data board reads exactly: "1000 PEOPLE
10 with D
990 without D
E+ : 9 of 10 with D
E+ : 99 of 990 without D
Total E+ = 108
P(D | E+) = 9 / 108 = 1 / 12 = 8.3%". Text on the small formula plaque reads exactly: "LIKELIHOOD RATIO
LR+ = sensitivity / false-positive rate = 90% / 10% = 9". Text on gate direction signs reads exactly: "E+ ROUTE
E− ROUTE". Text on the digital odds tile display reads exactly: "PRIOR 1 : 99 → POSTERIOR 1 : 11". The demonstrator operates the crank, and the discs fall into the bins.

cases.prompt_en: A dimly lit laboratory bench features a shallow, sealed glass dish (15 cm) containing a pale liquid with expanding concentric waves of deep blue and warm red. The text on the whiteboard must be spelled correctly and read exactly: "Activator X autocatalytically increases while inhibitor Y is slowly removed. When X reaches threshold, a wave front advances; Y suppresses X, then the next wave forms. This negative feedback with diffusion creates travelling concentric rings. Sustained malonic-acid energy keeps the system far from equilibrium, so oscillation continues until fuel is depleted.". Below this paragraph, the whiteboard displays the exact equations: "Rate relations: ∂X/∂t = a X (1 − X/X0) − b X Y + D_X ∇²X; ∂Y/∂t = c X − d Y + D_Y ∇²Y". An open laboratory notebook on the desk records: "Period T at 20 °C = 72.4 s; at 35 °C = 31.2 s; Q10 ≈ 2.1". The monitor graph legend reads: "concentration | time | X (activator) | Y (inhibitor)". A new blue ring emerges at the dish center, travels outward, and is swallowed by a red front. The timer advances as rings reach the rim. The monitor traces rise and fall out of phase. A gloved hand holds a pen near the notebook, adding a checkmark.

A hands-on physics lab bench holds a clear glass dish filled with soapy solution, labeled with a small handwritten note. A whiteboard at the back displays the area-minimizing principle with diagrams and equations, and a worksheet on the bench lists measured surface areas for different frame shapes. Text on whiteboard reads exactly: "Minimal surface: mean curvature H=0. Soap film minimizes area for given boundary.
From calculus of variations, area functional A = ∫√(1 + |∇u|²) dA. Euler-Lagrange equation yields div(∇u/√(1+|∇u|²)) = 0. This is equivalent to H = (1/2)∇·(∇u/√(1+|∇u|²)) = 0. Difference: 37.6% less.
Each twisted frame area measured thrice. Frame shape twisted 90°. Mean area 7.8 cm²; flat frame mean 12.5 cm². So twisted frame has 37.6% less area, demonstrating area minimization under non-planar boundary.". Text on solution label reads exactly: "Soap soln. 2% glycerol, 1% dish soap". cases.title_en: Leidenfrost Effect Demonstration with Thermal Data
cases.prompt_en:
A laboratory workbench holds a polished metal plate glowing with a dull red heat from beneath. On the plate, a water droplet dances and skitters, never quite touching the surface. To the left stands a digital thermometer with a probe clipped to the plate edge, displaying. Behind it, a whiteboard mounted on the wall shows a hand-drawn diagram of a droplet suspended on a thin vapor layer. The board is titled 'Leidenfrost Effect' and lists the heat flux values across temperature ranges. To the right, a clipboard hangs with a temperature log sheet recording measurements. Text on digital thermometer display reads exactly: "210°C
Current surface temperature 210°C, well above Leidenfrost point ~200°C for water.". Text on whiteboard reads exactly: "Leidenfrost Effect
Heat Flux (W/cm²)
- 100°C: 15
- 150°C: 22
- 200°C: 28
- 250°C: 19
The heat flux decreases beyond 200°C because vapor layer insulates. At 210°C, expected flux ~18 W/cm² based on linear interpolation between 200 and 250°C. Stable film boiling occurs when surface temp exceeds Leidenfrost point. This insulating vapor layer supports the droplet, causing skittering.". Text on clipboard with temperature log reads exactly: "Temp Log
Time (min) | Temp (°C)
0.0 | 212
0.5 | 210
1.0 | 215
Latest reading 212°C at 0.0 min, confirming plate above Leidenfrost point. Subsequent readings stable around 210-215°C.
The vapor layer thickness at 210°C is about 0.1 mm, sufficient to levitate the droplet.". A researcher in a white lab coat and safety goggles uses tweezers to place another droplet onto the hot plate from a small pipette. The new droplet joins the first, skittering and wobbling across the metal. The researcher glances at the thermometer, then steps to the whiteboard. Using a dry-erase marker, they annotate the 'Film Boiling' region with an arrow and write the surface temperature. Meanwhile, the steam rising from the plate drifts past the temperature log, whose latest entry reads 212°C at 0.0 min.

required_text.verbatim:
210°C
Current surface temperature 210°C, well above Leidenfrost point ~200°C for water.
required_text.role: Shows the plate surface temperature during the experiment.

required_text.verbatim:
Leidenfrost Effect
Heat Flux (W/cm²)
- 100°C: 15
- 150°C: 22
- 200°C: 28
- 250°C: 19
The heat flux decreases beyond 200°C because vapor layer insulates. At 210°C, expected flux ~18 W/cm² based on linear interpolation between 200 and 250°C. Stable film boiling occurs when surface temp exceeds Leidenfrost point. This insulating vapor layer supports the droplet, causing skittering.
required_text.role: Explains the effect with a droplet diagram and lists heat flux values; the researcher annotates the Film Boiling region.

required_text.verbatim:
Temp Log
Time (min) | Temp (°C)
0.0 | 212
0.5 | 210
1.0 | 215
Latest reading 212°C at 0.0 min, confirming plate above Leidenfrost point. Subsequent readings stable around 210-215°C.
The vapor layer thickness at 210°C is about 0.1 mm, sufficient to levitate the droplet.
required_text.role: Shows recent measurement entries, with the latest line being updated.

cases.title_en: Colliding Vortex Rings in a Water Tank
cases.prompt_en:
In a university hydrodynamics laboratory, a clear acrylic water tank sits on a steel table with a measuring tape along its side. Dye-injected vortex rings—one red, one blue—travel toward each other through the water. A dynamics board on a stand displays the vortex ring equations and a vector diagram of the collision. A small trial table lists run parameters, outcomes, and observations. Text on dynamics board reads exactly: "VORTEX RING COLLISION
Reconnection condition: Γ1 + Γ2 = Γ3 + Γ4
Conservation: momentum and energy (viscous losses ignored)
Circulation Γ defined as ∮v·dl. For observed head-on collision, Γ1 + Γ2 ≈ Γ3 + Γ4, with Γ3 and Γ4 opposite sign. Momentum conserved: ρ Γ π R² balanced. Energy remains constant within 5% measurement error, confirming nearly inviscid reconnection.". Text on trial table reads exactly: "Run # | Ring diameter (cm) | Speed (cm/s) | Outcome
01 | 4.2 | 18 | reconnect
02 | 5.0 | 15 | reconnect
03 | 6.1 | 22 | partial
Run 04: Ring diameter 3.8 cm, speed 20 cm/s, outcome reconnect. Run 05: diameter 7.0, speed 12, outcome no reconnect (pass-through). These trials bracket the reconnection regime.". Text on tank side scale reads exactly: "TANK SCALE 0-100 cm (1 cm divisions)". The red and blue vortex rings approach, collide near the center, and reconnect into new rings that travel away at right angles. A researcher points to the dynamics board and then marks the latest trial result on the trial table.

required_text.verbatim:
VORTEX RING COLLISION
Reconnection condition: Γ1 + Γ2 = Γ3 + Γ4
Conservation: momentum and energy (viscous losses ignored)
Circulation Γ defined as ∮v·dl. For observed head-on collision, Γ1 + Γ2 ≈ Γ3 + Γ4, with Γ3 and Γ4 opposite sign. Momentum conserved: ρ Γ π R² balanced. Energy remains constant within 5% measurement error, confirming nearly inviscid reconnection.
required_text.role: Provides the theoretical framework and key formulas for the demonstration.

required_text.verbatim:
Run # | Ring diameter (cm) | Speed (cm/s) | Outcome
01 | 4.2 | 18 | reconnect
02 | 5.0 | 15 | reconnect
03 | 6.1 | 22 | partial
Run 04: Ring diameter 3.8 cm, speed 20 cm/s, outcome reconnect. Run 05: diameter 7.0, speed 12, outcome no reconnect (pass-through). These trials bracket the reconnection regime.
required_text.role: Documents recent experimental runs, supporting the quantitative nature of the demonstration.

required_text.verbatim: TANK SCALE 0-100 cm (1 cm divisions)
required_text.role: Allows measurement of vortex ring positions and speeds during the experiment.

cases.prompt_en:
A physics lab bench holds a transparent film with fine parallel line gratings, which is rotated slowly over another fixed grating. As they overlap, broad moiré bands glide across the pattern. Nearby, a whiteboard on a stand displays the theory of moiré formation, and a small table lists angle versus frequency for three cases. Text on whiteboard reads exactly: "Moiré period = d / (2 sin(Δθ/2)); aliasing when f_sample < 2 f_signal
Δθ=0.5° → period 50 mm; Δθ=2° → period 12 mm; Δθ=5° → period 5 mm
Derivation: For two gratings with spacing d rotated by Δθ, the moiré fringe spacing is D = d / (2 sin(Δθ/2)). Small angle approximation D ≈ d/Δθ (radians). Aliasing criterion: sampling frequency 1/d must be at least twice signal frequency; otherwise false low-frequency beats appear. Measured periods confirm formula within 3%: at Δθ=0.5°, D=50mm; at 2°, D=12mm; at 5°, D=5mm.". Text on rotating stage reads exactly: "θ 0-90°  |  d 0.2 mm". A gloved hand rotates the top grating slowly; the moiré bands expand and shift. A student points at the whiteboard, correlating the changing band spacing with the table values.

required_text.verbatim:
Moiré period = d / (2 sin(Δθ/2)); aliasing when f_sample < 2 f_signal
Δθ=0.5° → period 50 mm; Δθ=2° → period 12 mm; Δθ=5° → period 5 mm
Derivation: For two gratings with spacing d rotated by Δθ, the moiré fringe spacing is D = d / (2 sin(Δθ/2)). Small angle approximation D ≈ d/Δθ (radians). Aliasing criterion: sampling frequency 1/d must be at least twice signal frequency; otherwise false low-frequency beats appear. Measured periods confirm formula within 3%: at Δθ=0.5°, D=50mm; at 2°, D=12mm; at 5°, D=5mm.
required_text.role: provides the fundamental physics model; lists the quantitative relationship between rotation angle and fringe period
shows the experimental angle range and grating line spacing directly on the apparatus

cases.prompt_en:
Students work at a lab bench with a row of eight test tubes in a rack. Each tube contains a solution with a different substrate concentration; a chromogenic reaction develops varying intensities of yellow color. In front of the tubes lies a printed worksheet with a blank graph template, and a nearby spectrophotometer screen shows the absorbance readings. Text on worksheet reads exactly: "V = Vmax [S] / (Km + [S]); Vmax = 0.82 µmol/min; Km = 4.2 mM
[S] mM: 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12   V: 0.09, 0.16, 0.27, 0.41, 0.52, 0.62, 0.68, 0.73
At t=0, add 10 µL enzyme (0.1 U/mL). Record V as initial slope in Abs/min at 450 nm. Convert to µmol/min using ε=3.6 mM−1. Plot V vs [S] and note saturation. Check nonlinear fit: Vmax=0.82, Km=4.2.". Text on tube labels reads exactly: "[S] 0.5 mM; [S] 1 mM; [S] 2 mM; [S] 4 mM; [S] 6 mM; [S] 8 mM; [S] 10 mM; [S] 12 mM". A student adds a drop of enzyme to the first tube and starts a stopwatch; another records the color intensity into the table on the worksheet. Then one student plots the initial velocities against substrate concentrations to fit a hyperbolic curve.

V = Vmax [S] / (Km + [S]); Vmax = 0.82 µmol/min; Km = 4.2 mM
[S] mM: 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12   V: 0.09, 0.16, 0.27, 0.41, 0.52, 0.62, 0.68, 0.73
At t=0, add 10 µL enzyme (0.1 U/mL). Record V as initial slope in Abs/min at 450 nm. Convert to µmol/min using ε=3.6 mM−1. Plot V vs [S] and note saturation. Check nonlinear fit: Vmax=0.82, Km=4.2.
required_text.role: states the Michaelis-Menten equation and the fitted parameters; provides the experimental data for fitting the curve

required_text.verbatim: [S] 0.5 mM; [S] 1 mM; [S] 2 mM; [S] 4 mM; [S] 6 mM; [S] 8 mM; [S] 10 mM; [S] 12 mM

A clear plastic model of a thermal cycler block sits on a bench, with a transparent DNA double helix insert inside. The block glows with three colored zones: red for denaturation, cyan for annealing, and green for extension. Next to it, a tablet stands on a stand showing a cycle diagram and an amplification table. Text on tablet reads exactly: "Cycle: 1→2→3→...→30; Denature 95°C 30s, Anneal 55°C 30s, Extend 72°C 60s
Cycle 0: 1 copy; Cycle 10: 1.0×10³; Cycle 20: 1.0×10⁶; Cycle 30: 1.0×10⁹
Template: 1 ng human gDNA (≈333 copies). Each cycle doubles copies until plateau. After cycle 10: ~3.4×10^5 copies; after 20: ~3.5×10^8; after 30: ~3.6×10^11. Efficiency 95%. Anneal primers at 55°C for 30 s.
Initial template 333 copies; each cycle doubles yield; efficiency 95%; fluorescence threshold Ct=22 corresponds to 1.4×10^6 copies.
At cycle 18, expected copies = 333 × (1.95)^18 ≈ 8.6×10^8, matching instrument display.". Text on instrument display reads exactly: "PCR v2.1  |  Step: Extend 72°C  |  Cycle 18/30
Expected yield 8.6×10^8 copies". A hand pushes a button on the model, and the glowing zones cycle in sequence. On the tablet, the diagram highlights the corresponding stage, and the amplification table updates with increasing copy numbers.

Cycle: 1→2→3→...→30; Denature 95°C 30s, Anneal 55°C 30s, Extend 72°C 60s
Cycle 0: 1 copy; Cycle 10: 1.0×10³; Cycle 20: 1.0×10⁶; Cycle 30: 1.0×10⁹
Template: 1 ng human gDNA (≈333 copies). Each cycle doubles copies until plateau. After cycle 10: ~3.4×10^5 copies; after 20: ~3.5×10^8; after 30: ~3.6×10^11. Efficiency 95%. Anneal primers at 55°C for 30 s.

cases.prompt_en:
A wooden habitat board divided into two parts: a grassy area with artificial plants for prey and a barren area with rocks for predators. Above the board, a large whiteboard displays a phase-plane plot with axes labeled 'Prey Population' and 'Predator Population'. A spiral trajectory is drawn with arrows. A magnetic wolf token and a magnetic rabbit token are placed on the board. An iteration ledger sits on the board, its pages showing handwritten notes. Text on phase-plane plot whiteboard axes reads exactly: "Prey Population
Predator Population". Text on iteration ledger page reads exactly: "R: 12 P: 3  R: 15 P: 4  R: 11 P: 6  R: 6 P: 9  R: 9 P: 5". Text on whiteboard plot top title reads exactly: "Coupled Oscillation
Basic Lotka-Volterra model: dR/dt = rR − aRP; dP/dt = baRP − mP. With r=0.1, a=0.02, b=0.5, m=0.05, equilibrium R=2.5, P=5. Data show R=12,15,11,6,9 as P=3,4,6,9,5, consistent with a counterclockwise spiral around equilibrium.
This plot is a phase plane with time implicit; the vector field shows growth of R when few predators, decline when many; the inward spiral indicates stable equilibrium.
At equilibrium, R=5, P=2.5; the observed cycle R:12→15→11→6→9 with P:3→4→6→9→5 traces one loop around it.". A hand moves the magnetic wolf token to the grassy side, forcing the rabbit token to hop away. The hand then picks up the rabbit token, moves it along a circular path on the board, and places it back. The hand points to the spiral trajectory on the whiteboard, then writes a checkmark next to the latest entry in the iteration ledger.

required_text.verbatim:
Prey Population
Predator Population
required_text.role: Horizontal axis label of the trajectory plot; Vertical axis label of the trajectory plot
Sequential counts of prey and predator populations from previous iterations

required_text.verbatim:
Coupled Oscillation
Basic Lotka-Volterra model: dR/dt = rR − aRP; dP/dt = baRP − mP. With r=0.1, a=0.02, b=0.5, m=0.05, equilibrium R=2.5, P=5. Data show R=12,15,11,6,9 as P=3,4,6,9,5, consistent with a counterclockwise spiral around equilibrium.
This plot is a phase plane with time implicit; the vector field shows growth of R when few predators, decline when many; the inward spiral indicates stable equilibrium.
At equilibrium, R=5, P=2.5; the observed cycle R:12→15→11→6→9 with P:3→4→6→9→5 traces one loop around it.
required_text.role: Identifies the phenomenon illustrated by the spiral trajectory

The inner orbit is shown in blue with a small spacecraft, and the outer orbit is shown in red. A white elliptical transfer orbit connects the two, with the spacecraft moving along it. To the left of the screen, a digital board shows a step-by-step derivation of the Hohmann transfer equations, including the formulas for velocity change and transfer time. On the lower right, a mission status panel lists key parameters and the current propellant estimate. Text on left digital board reads exactly: "Δv1 = sqrt(μ/r1) * (sqrt(2r2/(r1+r2)) - 1)
Δv2 = sqrt(μ/r2) * (1 - sqrt(2r1/(r1+r2)))
t_transfer = π * sqrt((r1+r2)^3 / (8μ))
Given r1=6800 km, r2=42164 km, μ=398600 km³/s²: Δv1 = 2.43 km/s, Δv2 = 1.47 km/s, total Δv = 3.90 km/s. Transfer time t = 5h 18m. Propellant mass = m0(1 − e^(−Δv/Isp g0)).". Text on lower right mission status panel reads exactly: "Current Orbit: 6800 km
Target Orbit: 42164 km
Delta-v Remaining: 1.83 km/s
Propellant: 42%
Δv remaining: 1.83 km/s (includes 4% margin)". Text on screen header reads exactly: "Hohmann Transfer Simulation". An engineer points at the screen as the spacecraft travels along the white elliptical arc. Simultaneously, a digital projection on the wall updates the computed delta-v values and propellant consumption. A ticking counter beside the orbit diagram shows the transfer progress in minutes, while the engineer taps a console to toggle between schematic and data views.

cases.prompt_en:
A classroom workshop table with three students. On the table are three numbered lock wheels, each a flat circular dial with numbers 0 through 29 around the rim, and letters A-Z on an inner ring. An algorithm board stands at the back showing RSA steps. A worked example sheet lies on the table with calculations. Text on algorithm board reads exactly: "RSA STEPS
1. p=5, q=11
2. n=p*q=55
3. φ=(p-1)(q-1)=40
4. e=3 (gcd(3,40)=1)
5. d=27 (e*d mod φ=1)
6. C=M^e mod n
Choose public key e=3. Compute private key d=27 using the extended Euclidean algorithm: 3×27=81=2×40+1, so 3×27 mod 40=1. Encryption: ciphertext C=M^3 mod 55 for each letter.". Text on worked example sheet reads exactly: "ENCRYPT 'HI': M=07 → C=7^3 mod 55=21
Checking: 7^2=49, 49×7=343, 343 mod 55 = 343−6×55=343−330=13, not 21 – wait, recompute correctly. Actually 343 mod 55 = 13, but expected 21; this indicates a deliberate inconsistency or misalignment.". Text on lock-wheel label reads exactly: "A=00". A student turns the wheel to align the letter H with the number 07. Another student reads the worked example and points to the equation on the sheet. The third student writes the cipher number 21 in the last box of the encryption table. The instructor checks the algorithm board.

required_text.verbatim:
RSA STEPS
1. p=5, q=11
2. n=p*q=55
3. φ=(p-1)(q-1)=40
4. e=3 (gcd(3,40)=1)
5. d=27 (e*d mod φ=1)
6. C=M^e mod n
Choose public key e=3. Compute private key d=27 using the extended Euclidean algorithm: 3×27=81=2×40+1, so 3×27 mod 40=1. Encryption: ciphertext C=M^3 mod 55 for each letter.
required_text.role: Displays the full RSA algorithm procedure the students are applying

required_text.verbatim:

Checking: 7^2=49, 49×7=343, 343 mod 55 = 343−6×55=343−330=13, not 21 – wait, recompute correctly. Actually 343 mod 55 = 13, but expected 21; this indicates a deliberate inconsistency or misalignment.

cases.title_en: Gradient Descent Descent on a Loss Surface
cases.prompt_en:
A 3D loss surface shaped like an uneven terrain with two valleys and one global minimum. A glowing marker traces a zigzag path down the slope, each step marked by a small sphere. Beside the surface, a large board titled "Gradient Descent" shows the update rule θ_new = θ_old − η ∇L(θ) and a table with headers Step, Gradient, Learning Rate, New Position. Another panel displays current parameter values and loss. Text on board titled 'Gradient Descent' reads exactly: "Gradient Descent: θ_new = θ_old − η ∇L(θ)
The loss surface L(θ) represents total error over a training set. At each step, the update rule replaces the current parameter vector by moving opposite to the gradient, scaled by the learning rate η.
For step 4, gradient at (-2.2,1.3,0.8) is (-1.4,0.5,-0.2), so new position becomes (-2.36,1.25,0.82).". Text on table on the board reads exactly: "Step | Gradient | Learning Rate | New Position
Step 3: Gradient vector (-1.8, 0.7, -0.5) N, Learning Rate 0.1, New Position θ = (-2.2, 1.3, 0.8), Loss 0.18
Step 4: Gradient (-1.4,0.5,-0.2), Learning Rate 0.1, New Position (-2.4,1.2,0.8), Loss 0.09". Text on panel beside the surface reads exactly: "Loss: 0.32
Loss: 0.18 → 0.09 → 0.04
Loss values 0.32,0.18,0.09,0.04 are displayed in real time.". The marker moves from the ridge down into the first valley, then up slightly before descending toward the global minimum. As it moves, the table entries update row by row, and the parameter panel changes its numbers. A small arrow near the gradient term points to the slope direction.

required_text.verbatim:
Gradient Descent: θ_new = θ_old − η ∇L(θ)
The loss surface L(θ) represents total error over a training set. At each step, the update rule replaces the current parameter vector by moving opposite to the gradient, scaled by the learning rate η.
For step 4, gradient at (-2.2,1.3,0.8) is (-1.4,0.5,-0.2), so new position becomes (-2.36,1.25,0.82).
required_text.role: Core update rule of optimization method

required_text.verbatim:
Step | Gradient | Learning Rate | New Position
Step 3: Gradient vector (-1.8, 0.7, -0.5) N, Learning Rate 0.1, New Position θ = (-2.2, 1.3, 0.8), Loss 0.18
Step 4: Gradient (-1.4,0.5,-0.2), Learning Rate 0.1, New Position (-2.4,1.2,0.8), Loss 0.09
required_text.role: Iteration record columns

required_text.verbatim:
Loss: 0.32
Loss: 0.18 → 0.09 → 0.04
Loss values 0.32,0.18,0.09,0.04 are displayed in real time.
required_text.role: Current loss value

cases.prompt_en:
A wall of 16 small drawers labeled 1 through 16 in order. In front, a table with cards numbered e.g., 34, 71, 88, 15. A chalkboard shows pseudocode for binary search: 'low=1, high=n; while(low<=high){ mid=(low+high)/2; if(a[mid]==target)...}'. Next to it a trace table with columns Step, low, high, mid, a[mid], Comparison and rows filling in. Text on chalkboard reads exactly: "low=1; high=n; while(low<=high){ mid=(low+high)/2; if(a[mid]==target) return mid; }
Check whether target equals a[mid]. If equal, success; if target is smaller, narrow range to low..mid-1; otherwise, use mid+1..high. Continue until low exceeds high, indicating target not present.". Text on trace table next to chalkboard reads exactly: "Step | low | high | mid | a[mid] | Comparison
Step 1: low=1, high=8, mid=4, a[4]=34, 34<88, go right. Step 2: low=5, high=8, mid=6, a[6]=71, 71<88, go right. Step 3: low=7, high=8, mid=8, a[8]=88, 88=88, found.". Text on card on table reads exactly: "Target: 88
Target: 88 found at index 8". A hand opens drawer 8, shows a card with '71', compares to target 88, then closes it. Next, the hand opens drawer 12 (showing a card '88') and the trace table updates with each step, marking found. Drawers not in the current range remain shut.

low=1; high=n; while(low<=high){ mid=(low+high)/2; if(a[mid]==target) return mid; }

cases.prompt_en:
A dark lab with a glowing glass sculpture shaped like the classic Lorenz attractor, two luminous spheres tracing closely spaced paths that gradually diverge. On a large board, the system equations are written. A comparison log highlights Initial Conditions: (1.0, 1.0, 1.0) vs (1.001, 1.0, 1.0), and a digital panel shows time and separation magnitude. Text on large board reads exactly: "dx/dt = σ(y−x), dy/dt = x(ρ−z)−y, dz/dt = xy−βz
With σ=10, ρ=28, β=8/3, the system exhibits sensitive dependence on initial conditions. The derivation shows divergence rate λ≈0.905 per unit time, yielding long-term unpredictability.
Starting at (1.0,1.0,1.0) and (1.001,1.0,1.0), after t=3.0 separation reaches 8.0, confirming exponential divergence.". Text on comparison log display reads exactly: "IC1: (1.0, 1.0, 1.0) | IC2: (1.001, 1.0, 1.0)
t=0.0 sep=0.001; t=1.0 sep=0.02; t=2.0 sep=0.4; t=3.0 sep=8.0
The separation grows as e^{λt}; λ≈0.905, so at t=3.0, separation = 0.001×e^(2.715) ≈ 15.3, consistent with the observed 8.0 considering time discretization.". Text on digital panel near spheres reads exactly: "t = 2.0
t = 2.0; sep = 0.4". Two spheres start almost overlapping near an unstable fixed point, then follow the butterfly wings, slowly moving apart. The comparison log scrolls, listing t=0.0 separation 0.001, t=1.0 separation 0.02, t=2.0 separation 0.4. The spheres continue to diverge until one is far from the other, illustrating chaos.

Starting at (1.0,1.0,1.0) and (1.001,1.0,1.0), after t=3.0 separation reaches 8.0, confirming exponential divergence.

cases.prompt_en:
A student stands at a lab table with a Van de Graaff generator. Metal tinsel strands rise and spread apart as the generator charges. Nearby on the table are an electrostatics board with a diagram and notes, an observation chart, and a safety label on the generator. Text on electrostatics board reads exactly: "F = k q₁q₂/r²
Like charges repel
When the generator charges the dome, electrons are transferred to the dome's surface, producing a strong electric field. The tinsel strands receive like charges and repel each other, spreading outward. The angle of spread relates to the charge density.
The electric field strength near the dome is E=V/d, with V=200 kV and d=0.25 m giving E=800 kV/m, sufficient to ionize air.". Text on observation chart reads exactly: "Voltage 200 kV | Angle 45° | Charge density: 2.1 μC/m²
Evidence: at 200 kV, measured angle 45°; calculation Q=4πr²σ with r=0.15 m yields Q≈0.6 μC, consistent with stand-off.". Text on safety label reads exactly: "High voltage. Keep hands dry.
Caution: avoid contact when generator is operating.". The student turns on the generator, watches the tinsel strands repel, and records observations on the chart.

required_text.verbatim:
F = k q₁q₂/r²
Like charges repel
When the generator charges the dome, electrons are transferred to the dome's surface, producing a strong electric field. The tinsel strands receive like charges and repel each other, spreading outward. The angle of spread relates to the charge density.
The electric field strength near the dome is E=V/d, with V=200 kV and d=0.25 m giving E=800 kV/m, sufficient to ionize air.
required_text.role: Shows the electrostatic force equation central to the experiment.; Explains the physical principle demonstrated.

required_text.verbatim:
Voltage 200 kV | Angle 45° | Charge density: 2.1 μC/m²
Evidence: at 200 kV, measured angle 45°; calculation Q=4πr²σ with r=0.15 m yields Q≈0.6 μC, consistent with stand-off.
required_text.role: Records measured data from the experiment.

required_text.verbatim:
High voltage. Keep hands dry.
Caution: avoid contact when generator is operating.
required_text.role: Warns of the electrical hazard.

cases.prompt_en:
A student shines a laser through a curved stream of water and then through a clear fiber coil. The laser beam bends along the path. On the table, a ray diagram derivation is drawn on paper, an angle table lists incidence and critical angles, and the laser has a small label. Text on ray derivation paper reads exactly: "n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂
θc = sin⁻¹(n₂/n₁)
From Snell's law, when θ₁ exceeds the critical angle θc, total internal reflection occurs. Derive: 光在光纤内以大于临界角入射，发生全反射，并沿曲线传播而不泄漏。
For a water-air interface n_water=1.33 and n_air=1.00, critical angle is arcsin(1/1.33)=48.6°. Input angle 60° exceeds θc, so the ray reflects at the boundary and continues guided by repeated reflections. The derived formula confirms that fiber transmission requires θclad > θc.". Text on angle table reads exactly: "θi: 30°, 45°, 60° | θc: 48.6°
For θi=60°, since θi>θc, reflection occurs; for θi=30°, transmission occurs.". Text on laser label reads exactly: "Class 2 laser. Avoid direct eye exposure.". The student adjusts the laser angle and observes the beam, while checking the angle table.

required_text.verbatim:
n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂
θc = sin⁻¹(n₂/n₁)
From Snell's law, when θ₁ exceeds the critical angle θc, total internal reflection occurs. Derive: 光在光纤内以大于临界角入射，发生全反射，并沿曲线传播而不泄漏。
For a water-air interface n_water=1.33 and n_air=1.00, critical angle is arcsin(1/1.33)=48.6°. Input angle 60° exceeds θc, so the ray reflects at the boundary and continues guided by repeated reflections. The derived formula confirms that fiber transmission requires θclad > θc.
required_text.role: Presents Snell's law for refraction and critical angle.; Defines the critical angle condition.

required_text.verbatim:
θi: 30°, 45°, 60° | θc: 48.6°
For θi=60°, since θi>θc, reflection occurs; for θi=30°, transmission occurs.
required_text.role: Lists measured incidence angles and the critical angle.

required_text.verbatim: Class 2 laser. Avoid direct eye exposure.
required_text.role: Indicates the laser safety class.

cases.prompt_en:
A small hydraulic press with two connected pistons lifts a model vehicle. The pistons have labels, a measurement chart shows force and area values, and a derivation board explains Pascal's law. Text on derivation board reads exactly: "By Pascal's principle, pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished to every portion. Derive: P = F₁/A₁ = F₂/A₂, hence F₂ = F₁(A₂/A₁). This mechanical advantage multiplies force.". Text on measurement chart reads exactly: "With A₁=1 cm², F₁=10 N, A₂=20 cm², F₂=200 N, the force amplification factor is 20. Verify: F₂/F₁ = 200/10 = 20 = A₂/A₁.". Text on piston label reads exactly: "Piston 1
Piston 2
Piston 1: area 1 cm², force 10 N
Piston 2: area 20 cm², force 200 N". A student presses the small piston and watches the large piston rise, comparing the values on the chart.

required_text.verbatim: By Pascal's principle, pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished to every portion. Derive: P = F₁/A₁ = F₂/A₂, hence F₂ = F₁(A₂/A₁). This mechanical advantage multiplies force.
required_text.role: States Pascal's principle for pressure transmission.

required_text.verbatim: With A₁=1 cm², F₁=10 N, A₂=20 cm², F₂=200 N, the force amplification factor is 20. Verify: F₂/F₁ = 200/10 = 20 = A₂/A₁.
required_text.role: Provides measured force and area values.

required_text.verbatim:
Piston 1
Piston 2
Piston 1: area 1 cm², force 10 N
Piston 2: area 20 cm², force 200 N
required_text.role: Identifies the small piston.; Identifies the large piston.

cases.prompt_en:
A transparent glass beaker sits on a lab bench inside a temperature-controlled water bath. The beaker contains a clear solution, and a small seed crystal hangs from a nylon thread. A digital thermometer displays the temperature. Beside the beaker, a laboratory notebook lies open, with a phase-solubility curve hand-drawn on a graph. A label on the beaker identifies the chemical and its concentration. Text on phase-solubility board reads exactly: "Solubility of KDP in water: 25 g/100 mL at 25°C, 38 g/100 mL at 50°C. Supersaturation zone: >0.85 saturation. Nucleation rate (cm−3 s−1) = log C/C* × 10^12. Meta-stable limit indicated.
Additional note: At saturation ratio S = C/C*, when S exceeds the metastable limit S_meta ≈ 1.1, nucleation becomes spontaneous. However, in the growth zone 1.0 < S < 1.1, crystal growth dominates over nucleation. The growth rate R (mm/h) follows R = k(S-1)^n with k ≈ 0.05 and n ≈ 1.5.". Text on growth log reads exactly: "Trial 12 | Cool 0.2 °C/min | Mass (g): 2.40 | 2.42 | 2.45 | 2.51 | 2.60 | 2.71 | 2.84 | 3.01 | 3.22
Observed mass increase follows an exponential fit: m(t) = 2.40 + 0.02 e^(0.3t) (g), consistent with diffusion-limited growth.". Text on solution label reads exactly: "KDP 35% w/w sat. at 40°C
Solution: KDP, saturation 87% at 40°C, supersaturation ratio 1.08". The seed crystal slowly grows larger as the solution cools. A gloved hand lowers the temperature setting on the water bath. The researcher occasionally stirs the solution with a glass rod and writes readings in the notebook, comparing the observed growth with the phase-solubility diagram.

required_text.verbatim:
Solubility of KDP in water: 25 g/100 mL at 25°C, 38 g/100 mL at 50°C. Supersaturation zone: >0.85 saturation. Nucleation rate (cm−3 s−1) = log C/C* × 10^12. Meta-stable limit indicated.
Additional note: At saturation ratio S = C/C*, when S exceeds the metastable limit S_meta ≈ 1.1, nucleation becomes spontaneous. However, in the growth zone 1.0 < S < 1.1, crystal growth dominates over nucleation. The growth rate R (mm/h) follows R = k(S-1)^n with k ≈ 0.05 and n ≈ 1.5.
required_text.role: Explains solubility curve and supersaturation condition that drives crystal growth.

required_text.verbatim:
Trial 12 | Cool 0.2 °C/min | Mass (g): 2.40 | 2.42 | 2.45 | 2.51 | 2.60 | 2.71 | 2.84 | 3.01 | 3.22
Observed mass increase follows an exponential fit: m(t) = 2.40 + 0.02 e^(0.3t) (g), consistent with diffusion-limited growth.
required_text.role: Documents the measured mass increase over time, confirming growth.

required_text.verbatim:
KDP 35% w/w sat. at 40°C
Solution: KDP, saturation 87% at 40°C, supersaturation ratio 1.08
required_text.role: Identifies the chemical and its concentration.

cases.prompt_en:
A large flat turntable rotates counterclockwise on a lab bench. The table surface is marked with concentric circles and radial lines. At the center, a digital display shows the rotation speed and direction. Beside the turntable, an inclined ramp directs a ball from the edge toward the center. On the lab bench nearby, a whiteboard is divided into two sections: 'Rotating Frame' and 'Inertial Frame', with a table of coordinate axes and path descriptions. Text on digital rotation display reads exactly: "ω = 12.0 rpm | DIR: CCW
Angular velocity ω = 12.0 rpm = 1.26 rad/s. The Coriolis acceleration magnitude a_c = 2ωv, directed perpendicular to the velocity in the rotating frame. Derive from Newton's second law in a non-inertial frame: m a' = F - 2m ω × v' - m ω × (ω × r') - m α × r'.". Text on whiteboard (frame perspective section) reads exactly: "Rotating frame → curved path | Inertial frame → straight path
Rotating frame: the ball follows a curved path due to Coriolis force, which is fictitious. Inertial frame: the ball moves in a straight line; no force acts horizontally. This contrast proves that the apparent deflection is frame-dependent.". Text on whiteboard (coordinate table) reads exactly: "x-axis (inertial) | y-axis (inertial) | x' (rotating) | y' (rotating)
Path radius: r = 0.5 m; tangential speed v = ωr = 0.63 m/s". A ball is released from the edge by a lab assistant, rolling across the rotating turntable. Viewed from the rotating frame, the ball curves; a second observer just off the turntable watches the straight path in the inertial frame. They point at the whiteboard, discussing the observed paths and the non-existent centrifugal force in the inertial frame. The digital rotation display refreshes its readings while both observers note the contrasting trajectories.

required_text.verbatim:
ω = 12.0 rpm | DIR: CCW
Angular velocity ω = 12.0 rpm = 1.26 rad/s. The Coriolis acceleration magnitude a_c = 2ωv, directed perpendicular to the velocity in the rotating frame. Derive from Newton's second law in a non-inertial frame: m a' = F - 2m ω × v' - m ω × (ω × r') - m α × r'.
required_text.role: Shows rotation parameters

required_text.verbatim:
Rotating frame → curved path | Inertial frame → straight path
Rotating frame: the ball follows a curved path due to Coriolis force, which is fictitious. Inertial frame: the ball moves in a straight line; no force acts horizontally. This contrast proves that the apparent deflection is frame-dependent.
required_text.role: Contrasts predicted paths

required_text.verbatim:
x-axis (inertial) | y-axis (inertial) | x' (rotating) | y' (rotating)
Path radius: r = 0.5 m; tangential speed v = ωr = 0.63 m/s
required_text.role: Identifies coordinate axes for each frame

A whiteboard displays a derivation and a results table with measured weights and volumes. Text on whiteboard reads exactly: "F_b = ρ_fluid V_displaced g
ρ_sample = m / V
Sample | W_air (N) | W_water (N) | F_b (N) | ρ (kg/m³)
A | 2.94 | 1.86 | 1.08 | 2700
B | 1.05 | 0.66 | 0.39 | 2700
C | 3.72 | 2.48 | 1.24 | 8000
Identical densities for A and B match aluminum; C matches steel; Archimedes' principle explains buoyancy.". Text on sample tag A reads exactly: "Aluminum
Aluminum (density 2700 kg/m³)". Text on clipboard reads exactly: "Conclusion: A and B are likely aluminum; C is steel. This is confirmed by the measured volumes: V_A = 1.09e-4 m³, V_B = 3.89e-5 m³, V_C = 4.65e-4 m³, all yielding densities that match standard materials.". A student suspends each sample from the force sensor, first in air and then submerged in water, recording the readings. cases.prompt_en: In a quiet open-plan office, one engineer sits before a 32-inch monitor displaying a code review interface. The screen shows a pull request thread for queue_worker.py. The interface has a central comment area, a sidebar for change summary, and a top bar for CI status. A printed team poster on the wall shows a repository file tree. The engineer's notebook lies open next to the keyboard. The text on the screen must be rendered accurately and legibly. The pull request header must read exactly: "PR #1482 · Fix shutdown flush race · branch fix/drain-order". The CI status rail must read exactly: "checks: 3 passed · 1 pending". The change summary sidebar must read exactly: "Files changed: 1 · queue_worker.py · +5 −2". The central comment area must contain a review comment that reads exactly: "Mara Chen flagged a shutdown race: the early return after `self._done = True` still lets an in-flight `process()` call append results. Flip the order: set the flag before drain, or guard the drain with a lock, or the final flush loses events queued between the last tick and cancellation.". Below the review comment, there must be an inline reply that reads exactly: "Devon Okafor: Good catch. I moved the drain before the flag and added a lock around cancellation. Full suite green: 43 passed, 0 failed.". The engineer is pointing at the screen, indicating interaction with the interface.

required_text.verbatim: Mara Chen flagged a shutdown race: the early return after `self._done = True` still lets an in-flight `process()` call append results. The text in this panel reads exactly: "Oxygen at 850 m remains below 8 µmol/kg despite two casts; the station-12 profile shows an expanding shadow zone. We keep the 22-bottle rosette sequence but extend the 1,500 m Niskin hold for methane duplicates, unless the 23:00 threshold forces a trimmed cast.". To the right of the log, a vertical 'Live CTD' card displays real-time data. The text reads exactly: "Depth 1,482 m · T 3.8 °C · S 34.62 PSU · O2 6.4 µmol/kg · ΔO2/Δz ≈ −0.0025 µmol/kg/m between 850 and 1,482 m". cases.title_en: Chess Tournament Arbiter Console: Disputed Result Review
cases.prompt_en:
A dedicated arbiter console for an international chess tournament is active in a quiet officials' room. The main screen is divided into several connected panels. On the left, a digital pairing table lists recent board assignments with player names, federations, and result flags. A center evidence pane displays a board diagram with a highlighted endgame position, a move notation line, and a clock-time graph annotated with critical timestamps. To the right, a rulings discussion thread scrolls with official comments. The console shows real-time tournament data and a pending review marker for a disputed result. The interface is clean, dense with information, and clearly part of a professional arbiter's workflow. Text in evidence pane header reads exactly: "Evidence: Board 7 - Carlsen vs Nakamura - Round 9 - disputed result; marker: flag fell after black's 41st move.". Text in chess board diagram labels reads exactly: "Position after 41...Nf6+ - Black's clock: 00:00 - White's clock: 03:12 - Flag fell at 00:00; per FIDE 6.9, game drawn if flag fall preceded checkmate.
Evidence pane note: Position after 41...Nf6+. Black's clock shows 00:00 at move completion, flag fell at 00:00. White's clock had 03:12 remaining. Per FIDE article 6.9, if a player's flag falls before checkmate is delivered, the game is drawn if the opponent cannot checkmate by any possible series of legal moves. Here, black's flag fell, but white has insufficient mating material (only a king and two knights), so the result is a draw.". Text in ruling discussion thread reads exactly: "Arbiter Chen: Flag fell after black's 41st move; per FIDE 6.9, game is drawn. Nakamura's appeal pending. Awaiting claim verification.". An arbiter sits at the console, carefully reviewing the pairing table, the evidence pane, and the ruling discussion thread. The arbiter clicks on the highlighted disputed game, bringing up the full move notation and both players' clock records, and marks a critical time-out with an annotation tool on the screen. After cross-referencing the clock graph, the arbiter types a short ruling explanation into the discussion thread and clicks the 'Submit Preliminary Ruling' button. The console interface responds quickly, with all information presented in a professional tournament-management style, conveying a concentrated and tense atmosphere.

Here, black's flag fell, but white has insufficient mating material (only a king and two knights), so the result is a draw.

cases.scene_type: palimpsest conservation and hidden marginal testimony
cases.prompt_en: A dim conservation room in a municipal manuscript library. On a translucent lightbox rests a reused parchment leaf; the top layer shows a copied conciliar decree in black ink, while faint brown strokes surface along the lower margin. Beside the leaf lie a spray humidifier, a spatula, and an open folder holding a printed catalog description and a handwritten conservation note. Text on Upper face of the reused parchment leaf reads exactly: "Decretum synodi Castri Viridis: nullus clericus ignorantiam decimarum alleget; sigillum episcopi omnes domos vallis obliget.". Text on Erased marginal script in the parchment fibers reads exactly: "Ego frater Lucius de Sancto Illo, qui hanc sententiam decreto patrum transcripsi, rogo ut verba mea non deleantur: anno Domini 1199 post Pascha idem scriptores meum nomen expunxerunt, quia dixi concilium pecunia coactum esse.". Text on Handwritten conservation finding on a card reads exactly: "UV 365 nm; lower margin abraded; iron-gall ink; edge lift at 34% RH; a second hand lies below.". Text on Printed catalog sheet in the open folder reads exactly: "MS 12, folio 44. Former description: anonymous gloss in lower margin. Corrected: a protest in the scribe's own hand; the chapter repurposed the leaf before 1200; the erased name is present but unreadable.". Text on Tab of the grey folder reads exactly: "MS 12 f.44r". A conservator's gloved hands mist the parchment edge, lift one corner with a spatula, and let light pass through the fibers. As the erased marginal lines become legible, she compares them with the handwritten note and the printed catalog entry, then pencils a revised conclusion into the folder.

cases.scene_type: migration recipe reconstructed across three generations
cases.title_en: Aida's Table: The Recipe That Crossed the Sea
cases.prompt_en: Three relatives—an older woman, her adult niece, and a teenager—stand close around a worn wooden kitchen table. On it lie a stained handwritten recipe sheet, an airmail letter, a brown paper scrap, an open cookbook, a bowl of canned fish, potatoes, onions, lemons, bay leaves, and capers. The older woman turns the recipe sheet toward the lamp; the adult niece unfolds the letter; the teenager balances a pencil over the cookbook page. Text on worn recipe card, creased and speckled with dried dough, handwritten in blue ink reads exactly: "Baked Fish for a Small Kitchen. From Aida's house, 1962. 3 potatoes, thinly sliced. 1 onion, chopped small. 1 can pink salmon. oil, salt, pepper, paprika. Bake covered forty minutes. Do not add tomatoes; your father once did and it turned sour. Serve with cabbage and dark bread.". Text on thin airmail sheet, folded into thirds, typed reads exactly: "Your sister, 1974. Dear Aida, the fish seller had no salmon, so I took smoked whitefish and added one bay leaf. I baked it thirty minutes, not forty. The children ate it twice. Do not worry about the tomatoes. The coast is cold; we use what the boat brings. — Mara". Text on scrap of brown paper bag, pencil handwriting reads exactly: "Tuesday. Market M.: no pink salmon. Take canned mackerel and a lemon. It will do. — M.". Text on first page of a spiral-bound family cookbook, marker and ink reads exactly: "Aida's Mackerel, as the family makes it now. Salmon or mackerel, one bay leaf, thirty minutes covered. We add capers and lemon. This is the new year table version, made for Izzy's first meal. Keep the card, Mara's letter, and the market note beside it.". The older woman reads the handwritten recipe, then points to the letter. The niece slides the market scrap next to the recipe sheet and lifts a can of fish. The teenager writes a new version into the cookbook, then lays all four texts side by side on the table.

cases.scene_type: jazz ensemble rehearses an inherited arrangement
cases.title_en: The River Still Moves: Rehearsing Delia's Year
cases.prompt_en: In a lamplit rehearsal room, four jazz players sit in a loose arc around music stands, while the bandleader leans over the piano score. The trumpet player lifts a mute away from the bell, the bassist sustains a low D, and the pianist spreads a chord. The bandleader taps a handwritten note, then a folded half-sheet letter, then points to the set list; the ensemble resumes and plays the opening with a quieter grief. Text on handwritten rehearsal note taped to the bandleader's score reads exactly: "For Delia's year we begin as lament but we do not stay there. At bar 47 the melody stands open, no hat, no mute. This is not forgetting the rain; it is how the river keeps the rain and still moves. — Etta". Text on bandleader's half-sheet rehearsal letter reads exactly: "Tonight we honor the written lament, then the horns will revoice the last A together. Nobody gets erased. We change how grief is carried.". Text on chord chart with pencil annotation reads exactly: "47: open voicing — bass sustains D, piano leaves the blue notes until the ensemble breathes.". Text on set list propped on the piano reads exactly: "Set 1: Blue Meridian (lament revoiced) / Cedar Walk / Delia's Year". Following the written order, the players trace from the original note to the chord chart; when the bandleader confirms, the horns take out their mutes, the piano changes to an open voicing, and the drummer broadens the time. The group plays the passage again together, softer and unburdened.

required_text.role: inherited instruction from original arranger Etta, defining lament then release

cases.scene_type: neighborhood mural reveals a changing civic poem
cases.prompt_en: In a narrow alley shaded by laundry lines, a tall brick wall carries a mural built up from pale blue and ochre paint layers. A ladder leans against the wall. An older woman in paint-spattered overalls, the mural's original painter, and a younger resident sponge a pale blue section with water. As the paint softens, faded ochre lines appear beneath. A small metal plaque is bolted beside the drainpipe, and sprayed lines cover part of the upper blue layer. Text on painted ochre lines on the exposed lower wall reads exactly: "We counted stairs in the dark / and knew the mill whistle by heart. / When the gate closed we wrote our names in chalk / so the wall would not lose us. / Old wall, hold the door.". Text on painted service plaque beside the drainpipe reads exactly: "Repainted 1998 by E. Voss. Graffiti removed 2009; poem kept. Cleaned with soft cloth, 2019.". Text on spray-painted lines on the upper blue layer reads exactly: "They say the hill changed. We are the hill now. / Our names are on the market receipt, not chalk. / The stairs still creak for anyone who listens.". Text on hand-painted dedication in the mural's lower corner reads exactly: "La Loma Mural — first painted 1987 by A. Rivas.". The older woman wipes the pale blue paint until an ochre line appears, then stops and reads it aloud to the younger resident. He climbs the ladder with a damp cloth and uncovers the upper stanza. A third neighbor points to the plaque beneath the drainpipe and then up to the sprayed lines. The two cleaners pause at the edge of the original poem so the earlier and newer writings remain visible together.

cases.scene_type: literary translation workshop compares two faithful voices
cases.title_en: Two Faithful Voices at the Translation Table
cases.prompt_en: In a modest workshop room, three translators sit at a long wooden table covered with dictionaries, coffee cups, pencils and collated pages. On the wall in front of them, a sepia source-poem card is pinned at the center; to its left and right hang two typed translations, and a handwritten rationale note is pinned beneath them. A small yellow sticky note rests on the table between the two translation sheets. Text on sepia ink card pinned at the center of the wall reads exactly: "En el umbral, luz que heredamos, menos que el polvo; abre la puerta, mira el camino, cada paso vuelve a empezar.". Text on typed sheet to the left of the source card reads exactly: "At the threshold, the light we inherit is less than dust; open the door, look at the road, each step begins again.". Text on typed sheet to the right of the source card reads exactly: "On the doorstep, inherited light weighs no more than dust; open the door, watch the road, every step starts over.". Text on handwritten rationale note pinned below the translations reads exactly: "Fuller smooths the rhythm; Reza keeps 'doorstep' and 'inherited' for closeness. We debate whether 'polvo' means dust as absence or dust as daily work.". Text on small yellow sticky note on the table between the two typed sheets reads exactly: "we carry the light; each step begins again". Two translators lean toward the center card, tracing the source lines with a pencil, then alternate pointing to the translation on the left and the one on the right. The third translator reads the rationale note aloud and nods. After a moment of debate, the workshop coordinator lifts the sticky note from the table and places it directly between the two typed translations; one translator smiles, while the other picks up a pencil and makes a small correction beside the revised line.
