cases.prompt_en: In a sunlit family living room opening onto a kitchen, a mother and two children are engaged in a birthday scavenger hunt. A large potted fern sits on a low wooden table. On the table, a large clipboard holds a white sheet with clearly legible black text: "Sunny's Birthday Hunt Rules — Follow the cards in rainbow order. Each card tells where the next one hides. If a card is missing, use the answer printed on the next envelope. Do not open the last envelope. Have fun!". Next to the clipboard, a wicker basket holds a wrapped present with a red ribbon; a small card tucked under the ribbon reads: "Happy Birthday, Sunny! Open last. Love, everyone.". On the kitchen counter, a small paper envelope is propped upright against a metal canister; the envelope clearly displays the text: "Envelope 2 — If the fern card is missing, use this answer: timer card under the tea towels.". A large hand-drawn map is taped to the refrigerator door, clearly displaying the text: "Room Hunt Map — Start at the shoe rack. Fern clue under the plant. Timer clue on the kitchen shelf. Mirror clue behind the hall mirror. Gift waits in the laundry basket.". A folded towel rests on the shelf beside the stove. The girl is lifting the fronds of the fern, looking disappointed. The boy points directly at the envelope on the counter. The mother looks from the clipboard to the map, tracing a route with her finger.

A clipboard holding the team gear roster hangs beside a corkboard with a handwritten ride-and-gear sheet. Near the back wall, a laundry bin has a note taped above it. Both duffels carry round tag cards. Text on clipboard with team gear roster reads exactly: "Sat 9 AM vs Fairview Tire. Tag bags by jersey number. Dana #8, Sam #11, Leo #23, Mei #27, Ravi #45, Jess #54. Check bag tag against jersey before loading. Return washed jerseys to bin.". Text on handwritten ride-and-gear sheet pinned to corkboard reads exactly: "Ride + Gear Sheet – Saturday. Car A (Sam): Dana, Leo. Carries bag #23. Car B (Mei): Ravi, Jess. Carries bag #27. Check tags before loading.". Text on note taped above laundry bin reads exactly: "Wash after Sunday, uniforms only. Hang #11 and #27. Tumble low #23. No towels.". Text on round tag card on the first duffel bag reads exactly: "LEO #23". Text on round tag card on the second duffel bag reads exactly: "MEI #27". The first duffel bag, tagged for Leo, is open to reveal a folded jersey with the number 27 (Mei's number) clearly visible. The second duffel bag, tagged for Mei, is open to reveal a folded jersey with the number 23 (Leo's number) clearly visible. A teammate points at the mismatched jersey in the first bag, highlighting the error.

required_text.verbatim: Sat 9 AM vs Fairview Tire. Tag bags by jersey number. Dana #8, Sam #11, Leo #23, Mei #27, Ravi #45, Jess #54. Check bag tag against jersey before loading. Return washed jerseys to bin.
required_text.role: Team gear roster establishes the rule that each bag tag must match the player's jersey number, making the swapped tags visible.

required_text.carrier: handwritten ride-and-gear sheet pinned to corkboard
required_text.verbatim: Ride + Gear Sheet – Saturday. Car A (Sam): Dana, Leo. Carries bag #23. Car B (Mei): Ravi, Jess. Carries bag #27. Check tags before loading.
required_text.role: Assigns each car a specific bag to carry, so correcting the bag tags also forces a correction on this sheet.

required_text.verbatim: Wash after Sunday, uniforms only. Hang #11 and #27. Tumble low #23. No towels.
required_text.role: Laundry handoff note reminds which uniform numbers need special care, keeping the corrected jersey numbers connected to the gear roster.

required_text.carrier: round tag card on the first duffel bag
required_text.verbatim: LEO #23
required_text.role: This tag claims the bag belongs to Leo, but the jersey inside shows Mei's number.

required_text.carrier: round tag card on the second duffel bag
required_text.verbatim: MEI #27
required_text.role: This tag claims the bag belongs to Mei, but the jersey inside shows Leo's number.

cases.scene_type: living-room stereo reconnection after a cabinet move
cases.prompt_en:
In a living room after a media cabinet has been moved, two housemates kneel among a stereo receiver, turntable, speakers and a box of disconnected leads. Masking-tape cable flags, a hand-drawn shelf diagram and a listening-test notebook lie open beside the cabinet. Text on hand-drawn reconnection map taped inside the cabinet door reads exactly: "STEREO RECONNECT AFTER MOVE
Turntable RCA → PHONO L/R
Thin black ground → GND screw
Blue pair → LEFT speaker red/black
White pair → RIGHT speaker red/black
Connect power last. Test at low volume before closing cabinet.". Text on masking-tape flags wrapped around the loose cable ends reads exactly: "BLUE = LEFT SPEAKER
WHITE = RIGHT SPEAKER
THIN BLACK = TURNTABLE GROUND
RCA RED = RIGHT / RCA WHITE = LEFT". Text on listening-test page open on the floor reads exactly: "TEST RECORD: SIDE A, TRACK 2
First check 19:40 — right channel only; hum present.
Correction — blue to LEFT; black to GND.
Second check 19:47 — both channels clear; hum gone.
Noor + Eli.". Text on small note tucked under the cabinet wheel lock reads exactly: "Before pushing cabinet back: photograph rear panel, leave 8 cm cable slack, lock both front wheels.". They trace each labeled lead against the diagram, discover that the left speaker and turntable ground were swapped during packing, reconnect both, then play the marked test record and write the result before pushing the cabinet back against the wall.

required_text.carrier: hand-drawn reconnection map taped inside the cabinet door
required_text.verbatim:
STEREO RECONNECT AFTER MOVE
Turntable RCA → PHONO L/R
Thin black ground → GND screw
Blue pair → LEFT speaker red/black
White pair → RIGHT speaker red/black
Connect power last. Test at low volume before closing cabinet.
required_text.role: defines each destination and the safe household reconnection order

required_text.carrier: masking-tape flags wrapped around the loose cable ends
required_text.verbatim:
BLUE = LEFT SPEAKER
WHITE = RIGHT SPEAKER
THIN BLACK = TURNTABLE GROUND
RCA RED = RIGHT / RCA WHITE = LEFT
required_text.role: identifies leads that look similar after the move

required_text.carrier: listening-test page open on the floor
required_text.verbatim:
TEST RECORD: SIDE A, TRACK 2
First check 19:40 — right channel only; hum present.
Correction — blue to LEFT; black to GND.
Second check 19:47 — both channels clear; hum gone.
Noor + Eli.
required_text.role: records the audible symptom, cable correction and confirmed result

required_text.carrier: small note tucked under the cabinet wheel lock
required_text.verbatim: Before pushing cabinet back: photograph rear panel, leave 8 cm cable slack, lock both front wheels.
required_text.role: prevents the reconnection from being hidden or strained again

cases.scene_type: craft club continues a shared project between meetings
cases.title_en: The Gingham Pocket Finds Its Seam
cases.prompt_en: Three friends in a small sewing circle gather around a pine worktable in a brightly lit living room. An unfinished quilted wall pocket lies spread across the table. A paper pattern is pinned to a corkboard, an open materials notebook sits to one side, a handwritten index card is propped against a mason jar, and a folded piece of blue gingham cloth carries a small paper tag. Text on Handwritten index card propped against a mason jar on the worktable reads exactly: "Maya, pocket 7 is washed and ready. I changed its seam allowance to 3/8 inch because the backing pulled. Please attach it before you add the border. I used the last of the natural thread. — Lena". Text on Open spiral notebook page with a materials ledger reads exactly: "Natural thread — used up, replace. Blue gingham — 1/2 yard left. Cotton batting — enough for two pockets. Red bias tape — 1 yard. Fine needles — check box.". Text on Small measurement note pinned to the paper pattern on the corkboard reads exactly: "Pocket 7 opening: 9 1/2 inches wide after 3/8 seam. Top edge slopes 1 inch. Match stripe at center.". Text on Small paper tag pinned to the folded blue gingham fabric reads exactly: "Pocket 7 — Lena — seam 3/8". The next maker reads the handwritten handoff note from the previous maker, lifts the tagged blue gingham fabric, compares it with the measurement note on the paper pattern, trims the seam allowance with scissors, then pins the piece onto the unfinished wall pocket before the border is added.

cases.scene_type: houseguest instructions resolve a key and pet mix-up
cases.title_en: The Key That Opens the Door
cases.prompt_en:
A small tiled entryway inside a home, featuring a mirror, a wooden console, and a half-open kitchen doorway. On the console sits a ceramic bowl containing two nearly identical brass keys: one with a red tape tab, the other with a blue tape tab. A white envelope is taped to the mirror. A handwritten index card is clipped to the kitchen gate. A printed recycling calendar is on the refrigerator door. A whiteboard hangs beside the coat hooks. Next to the doorway is a small wooden key rack with two hooks labeled 'FRONT / MAIL'.

The text on the white envelope taped to the mirror must read exactly: "Priya, welcome! The red-taped brass key opens the front door; the blue-taped one opens the mailbox. Walk in, then hang the red key on the hook labeled FRONT and put the blue key in the drawer marked MAIL. I won't be back until six. Keeper is in the kitchen."

The text on the handwritten index card clipped to the kitchen gate must read exactly: "Keeper stays in the kitchen. Don't let him past the gate. He gets his food at five."

The text on the printed recycling calendar on the refrigerator door must read exactly: "Recycling: Paper 2nd Tue; Glass 4th Fri; Green bin weekly. No bag ties."

The text on the whiteboard beside the coat hooks must read exactly: "Mara: back by 6, feed Keeper at 5. Don't wait up. Thanks!"

A guest lifts the envelope from the mirror and reads it. She uses the key with the red tape to unlock the entry door. She steps inside, hangs that key on the left hook of the small key rack, and places the blue-taped key in a drawer beneath the rack. She then reads the handwritten card clipped to the kitchen gate, checks the recycling calendar on the refrigerator, and reads the morning message left on the whiteboard near the coat hooks.

required_text.verbatim: Priya, welcome! The red-taped brass key opens the front door; the blue-taped one opens the mailbox. Walk in, then hang the red key on the hook labeled FRONT and put the blue key in the drawer marked MAIL. I won't be back until six. Keeper is in the kitchen.

required_text.form: handwritten morning message on a whiteboard
required_text.role: host's schedule reminder for the guest

required_text.verbatim: FRONT / MAIL

cases.scene_type: balcony seed swap matches packets to available pots
cases.title_en: The Tall Flower Gets the Wider Pot
cases.prompt_en: Two neighbors stand on a balcony where seed packets, plastic pots, a tape measure, and a watering can sit on a small metal table. One neighbor holds a clipboard up to the camera so the text is clearly legible; the paper reads exactly: "Seed Swap — Sat 10:30. Priya: BLT tomatoes (start in 3-inch cell, then 12-inch pot), purple basil (6-inch pot), cosmos (tall — 14-inch pot). Leo: dwarf sunflower (10-inch pot), arugula (window box). Swap: Priya takes sunflower, Leo takes tomatoes. Each waters other's pots for 5 days from Jul 3.". On the table, a cosmos seed packet stands upright with text printed clearly on the front reading exactly: "Cosmos 'Sensation' — tall, 4–6 ft, space 12–14 in, stake early, full sun.". Next to it, a tomato seed packet stands upright with text printed clearly on the front reading exactly: "BLT Tomato — 60 days, bush, one seed per 3-in cell, full sun, stake at 12 in.". A yellow sticky note attached to the handle of the watering can reads exactly: "Water: Mon/Wed/Fri, 1 cup each; tomato daily. Leo waters Priya's pots Jul 3–7; Priya waters Leo's Jul 8–12.". A masking-tape tag on a narrow pot reads exactly: "Basil only: cosmos moved to 14-in pot.". The neighbor holding the clipboard gestures toward the packets, while the other neighbor holds the watering can.

Leo: dwarf sunflower (10-inch pot), arugula (window box). Swap: Priya takes sunflower, Leo takes tomatoes. Each waters other's pots for 5 days from Jul 3.
required_text.role: records the agreed exchange and watering promise

cases.scene_type: household recycling disagreement becomes a clear agreement
cases.prompt_en: Two roommates stand in a narrow apartment recycling corner beside a stack of flattened paper items. A wooden clipboard with a new signed household rule hangs above three bins. A handwritten note is taped to the blue bin, and a small calendar hangs on the nearby fridge. One roommate lifts a stained take-out box out of the blue bin while the other pulls an old label off the same bin and replaces it with a freshly marked strip of tape. Text on Handwritten agreement clipped to a wooden clipboard above the recycling bins reads exactly: "RECYCLING RULE — We all agreed: sort once a week, follow each label, and when a bin feels uncertain, leave the item out. Questions go on the whiteboard. Signed: Mira, Dana, Leo.". Text on Handwritten contamination note taped to the front of the blue bin reads exactly: "HEADS UP — The greasy pizza box from Saturday spoiled the entire paper batch. Keep all food-stained cardboard out of this bin. Clean boxes can be flattened under the shelf.". Text on Revised homemade label on a strip of masking tape stuck to the blue bin reads exactly: "CLEAN CARDBOARD ONLY". Text on Small household recycling calendar on the fridge reads exactly: "Recycling pickup — Tuesday. Put bins out Monday night. Next pickup June 14.". Text on Taped labels on the paper, glass, and plastic bins reads exactly: "PAPER / GLASS / PLASTIC". One roommate removes the greasy take-out box named in the note and drops it into a kitchen trash bag. The other roommate writes a stricter description on a new label and presses it onto the blue bin. The third roommate taps the signed agreement and points to the calendar to confirm the next pickup day.

required_text.verbatim: RECYCLING RULE — We all agreed: sort once a week, follow each label, and when a bin feels uncertain, leave the item out. Questions go on the whiteboard. Signed: Mira, Dana, Leo.
required_text.role: Anchor: the shared rule that turns the disagreement into an agreement

cases.scene_type: family emergency kit is renewed from its own inventory
cases.title_en: The Orange Bin Gets Its Odd-Month Check
cases.prompt_en:
A mother and her teenage daughter are kneeling on the tiled floor of a hallway, working with a bright orange emergency bin. The daughter holds a fresh water pack and an oatmeal bar, placing them into the bin. The mother holds a clipboard and writes a check mark on a paper checklist. Their father stands nearby, holding a magnetic note he took from the refrigerator, reading the address aloud to the girls. 

Text on the Laminated inventory sheet clipped to the inside of the orange kit lid must read exactly: "Family Emergency Kit Inventory. Check odd months. Replace only if dated before July 2024 or tester says LOW. Last checked Jan 14. Replace now: 2 water pouches, 4 AA batteries, 1 oatmeal bar. Keep flashlight, whistle, dust mask."

Text on the Paper checklist on the clipboard the mother is holding must read exactly: "Checklist today: 2 water pouches, 4 AA batteries, 1 oatmeal bar. Done: water replaced, batteries tested. Still need: bar. Next check: May 3. If you take something, write here."

Text on the Laminated contact card fixed to the front of the orange bin must read exactly: "Meeting place: Elin's porch, 42 Birch Lane. Wait there until everyone checks in. Bring this kit only if you leave."

Text on the Magnetic note the father is holding (originally from the refrigerator) must read exactly: "Call Maya 555-0192 or Rowan 555-0147. Say: safe, no one hurt."

required_text.verbatim: Family Emergency Kit Inventory. Check odd months. Replace only if dated before July 2024 or tester says LOW. Last checked Jan 14. Replace now: 2 water pouches, 4 AA batteries, 1 oatmeal bar. Keep flashlight, whistle, dust mask.

required_text.role: Establishes the replacement rule and the list of items that must be changed in the kit.

required_text.verbatim: Checklist today: 2 water pouches, 4 AA batteries, 1 oatmeal bar. Done: water replaced, batteries tested. Still need: bar. Next check: May 3. If you take something, write here.
required_text.role: Records the replacements that have already been done and the item still needed.

required_text.carrier: Laminated contact card fixed to the front of the orange bin
required_text.verbatim: Meeting place: Elin's porch, 42 Birch Lane. Wait there until everyone checks in. Bring this kit only if you leave.

cases.scene_type: accessible guest-room setup follows a friend's preferences

cases.prompt_en:
A bright, tidy guest bedroom scene showing the completed setup. A bed with white linens is on the left. A window with closed blackout curtains is in the background. An armchair sits near the window, with a floor lamp placed beside it. A dresser with labeled drawers is on the right. A bedside tray with a water carafe and glass sits on a nightstand. A printed note is taped to the door, and a small chalkboard stands on the dresser. Put the floor lamp beside the armchair, not in the doorway. Move the folding chair to the hallway; it blocks the path. Close the blackout curtains after noon. Spare blanket in the bottom drawer. SHEETS

cases.scene_type: sleepover plan reconciles household rules and personal needs
cases.title_en: Sleepover Sort at the Kitchen Island
cases.prompt_en: A kitchen and the adjoining entryway on a Saturday afternoon. Two parents and three children gather around the kitchen island, where backpacks and snack containers are lined up. A clipboard rests on the island, a yellow sticky note is on the refrigerator door, a small whiteboard hangs on the wall, a pickup card stands on the entry table, and a labeled snack container waits near the fruit bowl. Text on clipboard with the Sleepover Plan reads exactly: "Saturday sleepover at the Harrisons. Drop-off 4:30, dinner 5:30, movie 7:00, lights out 9:30. Pickup Sunday by 9:00. Label bags and snacks. No nuts anywhere.". Text on folded permission note pinned to a backpack reads exactly: "Mina may stay until Sunday breakfast. Her inhaler is in the front pocket. Call us if she coughs. - Lena". Text on yellow sticky note on the refrigerator door reads exactly: "Leo: no dairy, oat milk ok. Ruby: no strawberries. Sesame-free for Aria.". Text on whiteboard on the kitchen wall reads exactly: "8:45 pajamas, 9:00 teeth, 9:15 story, 9:30 lights out. Boys in the living room, girls in the den.". Text on printed label on a snack container reads exactly: "Leo's snack – oat crackers and grapes". The host reads the permission note pinned to Mina's backpack, then places the backpack with the bags set for a 9:00 pickup. She checks the yellow sticky note, swaps Leo's snack for the labeled oat-cracker container, and taps the whiteboard bedtime plan while the children set out their pajamas on the sofa.

required_text.verbatim: Saturday sleepover at the Harrisons. Drop-off 4:30, dinner 5:30, movie 7:00, lights out 9:30. Pickup Sunday by 9:00. Label bags and snacks. No nuts anywhere.

required_text.verbatim: Leo: no dairy, oat milk ok. Ruby: no strawberries. Sesame-free for Aria.
required_text.role: Lists per-child food limits the host must follow when handing out snacks.

cases.scene_type: after-party leftovers and lost property find their owners
cases.prompt_en:

Leftover food containers sit across the counter; two similar gray scarves lie over a chair back. A paper schedule is taped to the refrigerator door, and sticky notes and tags are attached to dishes and belongings. Done Sat night: washing spoons, bagging bottles.
Sunday noon: Lin takes green curry, Maya takes lentil salad.
Unmarked red container is Sofia's coconut rice — taste first.

Priya lifts the lid of the unlabeled container, reads the sticky note inside, smells coconut milk, and matches it to the posted schedule for the rice. Lin compares the tag on one gray scarf to the posted schedule and confirms it is hers; Maya checks the other scarf without a stripe. Arturo labels a take-out bag for Sofia, and they pack the handoffs.

cases.prompt_en:

Taped to the wall above the windowsill is a hand-drawn care chart on lined paper, with columns for 'Pothos', 'Spider Plant', and 'Monstera'. A spiral notebook lies open on the sill beside the jars. Text on care chart taped to the wall reads exactly: "PLANT | WATER | LIGHT
Pothos | 1x wk | low
Spider | 2x wk | bright
Monstera | 1x wk | medium". Text on small handwritten label taped to a jar reads exactly: "Pothos — day 6". Text on open spiral notebook on windowsill reads exactly: "Oct 12
Pothos 3
Spider 2
Monstera 1
watered all
October 12 notes: Pothos roots from jar 1 reached 2 inches, moved to soil in small pot. Spider plant produced two new pups, placed one in fresh water jar. Monstera cutting has one root at 1 inch, keep in water until 3 roots form. Watered all jars with filtered water.". A young woman trims a leafy stem with scissors over the tray. She picks up a jar, tapes a small onto it, and places it back. Then she uncaps a marker, flips the notebook to a fresh page, and writes new entries under the date 'October 12', updating counts for each plant type.
